chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى صَالِحُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah narrated from Sulaymān ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَنْكِحُ جَارِيَةَ امْرَأَتِهِ ثُمَّ يَسْأَلُهَا أَنْ تَجْعَلَهُ فِي حِلٍّ فَتَأْبَى فَيَقُولُ إِذًا لَأُطَلِّقَنَّكِ وَ يَجْتَنِبُ فِرَاشَهَا فَتَجْعَلُهُ فِي حِلٍّ

translations.en: He was asked about a man who has intercourse with his wife's bondwoman, then asks her to place him in pardon, but she refuses. So he says, "Then I will surely divorce you," and he keeps away from her bed until she places him in pardon.

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ هَذَا غَاصِبٌ فَأَيْنَ هُوَ عَنِ اللُّطْفِ

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: "This is a usurper, so where is he from gentleness?"

en.summary: This hadith condemns a husband who pressures his wife into pardoning his wrongful conduct by threatening divorce and withholding conjugal relations. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام describes such behavior as coercive and devoid of gentleness, highlighting the ethical limits within marital relations.
en.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about a husband coercing his wife to pardon him by threatening divorce?

key_terms.جَارِيَةَ: a bondwoman owned by the wife
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: in a state of release or pardon from liability
key_terms.لَأُطَلِّقَنَّكِ: I will surely divorce you; a threat used as pressure
key_terms.فِرَاشَهَا: her bed, referring to marital intimacy
key_terms.غَاصِبٌ: one who usurps or wrongfully takes by force
